utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Ms. Motoike

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Groseva. Yesterday on page 4754 of the transcript, you were given an example of the members of the Lions and the signing of their employment document. Do you have any knowledge of how members of the Lions were contracted by the Ministry of Interior in 2001?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I informed you, I used to work for a while as an advisor in the legal department, and my knowledge regarding the employment procedure for any employee in the Ministry of Interior. So what is the procedure, how persons who have special powers are employed, how are people employed through the procedure with a public ad, so I could not say anything specific. Just what is the regular employment procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So if I'm understanding you correctly, you can't speak to, based on your own personal knowledge, you cannot speak to how the Lions were contracted by the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On pages 4754 through 4755 of yesterday's transcript, you also spoke of the disciplinary committee within the Ministry of Interior. To your knowledge, are all disciplinary issues sent to this particular committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Later on in the transcript of yesterday, you indicated on pages 4760 through 4761 that the documents produced by your particular commission could not be used in court as evidence. I'd like to ask you: If the information demonstrated misconduct by a particular Ministry of Interior employee, could the information contained in the documents by the commission have been used by Minister Kostov to initiate disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information had a sole purpose, that is, to inform the minister of the interior about the work of the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You indicated on page 4768 of yesterday's transcript, that it was then the minister who had the responsibility to decide what to do with the particular information the commission had gathered. To your knowledge, does the collective agreement allow the minister to forward information with respect to disciplinary issues?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the disciplinary responsibility proceedings are initiated by the direct superior of the officer who has abused the power of office or is involved in misconduct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So would you know, based on the knowledge that you have, whether or not the minister who came to information with respect to disciplinary issues could forward that information to the disciplinary committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If the information contained within the documents of your commission had shown that a crime may have occurred, could the minister have forwarded this particular information to the public prosecutor for further investigation?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this is not possible. For the 15 years of my career in the sector for analytics, an information has never been forwarded to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we please show what has been admitted as P00096. And, actually, could we go to the first page of this particular document initially. Perhaps the second page in Macedonian -- in the Macedonian and the first page in English. Thank you. I think that the translations are not exactly linked.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, on the left of your screen there is a language there in the Macedonian language. This is a -- this is basically the rule book for the Ministry of Interior. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could go to, please, page 15 of the Macedonian and the corresponding English page is at R042-4638-ET. It's at page 1 of that particular ERN range. And if we could zoom in actually on the Macedonian on the right side of the page, article. It actually should be the next page in Macedonian. Could we zoom in on Article 103 on the bottom of the left-hand side of the Macedonian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, this is from the Rule Book of the Ministry of Interior and I'd just like to point out the Article here on the bottom of the Macedonian page that is being shown to you. It's Article 103. And right above that in bold words it is says: "Initial evidence for a crime that has been committed." Then the Article goes on to provide: "When there exists grounds for suspecting that a crime which is prosecuted in the line of duty has been committed, the authorised officials take the necessary measures," and then it goes on to say what these measures are. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could turn, please to another Article which is Article 167 of this same rule book. It is located at page 24 of the Macedonian. The corresponding English translation is at R042-4646-ET. It's at page 3 in that particular range. If we could focus in on -- yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Ms. Groseva, I'd like to draw your attention to the bottom of the Macedonian page that is displayed before you. It's the top of the English. In bold words at number two it says: "Submission of the criminal report. Article 167." Then it goes on to read: "If on the basis of the collected information and other measures and actions taken for its confirmation and documentation, it is asserted that there exists grounds for suspicion that the crime which is prosecuted in the line of duty was committed, the authorised official composes a criminal report which is delivered to the competent public." And I believe the translation in English says "defender," but I believe that says "public prosecutor." Do you see that, Ms. Groseva?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And I know that you indicated to us today that you were not aware of any -- anything happening where information was then forwarded to the public prosecutor with respect to the commissions, but would you agree that these articles that I just read out to you do set forth some procedure that allow the submission of information to the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In these particular Articles, though, it allows for information to be submitted when a crime is suspected to the public prosecutor. Is that my reading? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are now speaking about the procedure where there is reasonable grounds to believe a crime has been committed. As I clarified, there is a special service, special unit in the ministry that pursuant to our organisational structure act undertakes these activities in cooperation with the judicial organs. Our committee gathered information on whether -- or actually what has happened at Skopje village Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001. I never performed operative duties but I will say again, an information, what you see here as a format of information submitted to you here, is not forwarded or not attached to any document in the correspondence with the court. I'm now speaking about the format of information that you have here in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And I guess I was asking you more about the general information, not necessarily the documents, but the information contained with those reports you generated. If that information contains some type of reasonable ground that a crime had been committed, could that information, not necessarily your documentation been forwarded to the public prosecutor for review?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, not. No. The procedure is completely different when one is acting based on reasonable grounds to believe a crime has been committed. The correspondence between the expert services and the competent courts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: But if there is reasonable suspicion that a crime has been committed, you agree that these Articles then allow the submission of information to the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can't really distinguish here what the notion information is. Information, as a document is also when an authorised officer goes and communicates verbally, orally with the public prosecutor to communicate the information to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So if an authorised officer within the Ministry of Interior had obtained information not information necessarily from your documents, had obtained just general information, you say that they could then go orally to the public prosecutor to communicate the information?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, we do not fully understand one another. What I'm saying is that the notion, information, information in this format that you have here is produced by the sector for analytics research and documentation is not forwarded to the court. And what is the format of the information oral in writing from the operative work you saw I'm working for 15 years in the analytics.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I guess I was using the term information and maybe that's where we're -- I'm miscommunicating. I'm asking about whether facts are known. If there are some facts indicating reasonable suspicion that a crime had been committed, an authorised officer then can go to the public prosecutor and report that orally. Is that my understanding?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to ask this of the authorised officers who work in -- at that issues in our ministry, since everything I say would be a conjecture.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. On page 4771, actually 4770 to 4771 of yesterday's transcript you were asked about a gentleman by the name of Risto Galevski, another man by the name of Goran Mitevski and Zivko Petrovski. And at that time you were in -- in the -- in the course of this questioning yesterday, you had indicated that these persons were on the commission in 2001 and that was based on a review of the document you saw yesterday. At that time on page 4772 of the transcript, you stated that Goran Mitevski and Risto Galevski in your opinion, were exceptional professionals. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What about Zivko Petrovski? What is your opinion with respect to Mr. Petrovski?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that my assessment comprised also Mr. Zivko Petrovski, considering that, as I clarified, he was the head of the department where I used to work for a while, so I hold the same opinion also of Mr. Zivko Petrovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. On page 4793 of yesterday's transcript and, actually, could we go to a document first? Could we please show P00251 which has been marked for identification this document, I believe, is under seal so I'd ask that it not be publicised. And, Ms. Groseva, this is now displayed in front of you on the screen, the cover page. This is the correspondence from Mr. Besim Ramicevic that we saw yesterday. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And specifically if we could turn to, please, page 2 in the English, and page 3 of the Macedonian, yesterday I believe this last paragraph which is the third full paragraph in English, and paragraph -- first full paragraph in the Macedonian, that paragraph which begins with: "The ministry possesses data that on 10 August 2001, approximately 20 people arrived at the Cair police station, the majority of whom were known perpetrators of criminal activities. They requested that they be issued weapons and uniforms, though Ljube Krstevski, the head of the Cair OVR, municipal military sector ordered that this not be allowed explaining that there were no weapons nor uniforms. He informed the administrator of this station the following day, 11 August 2001, by mobile phone that an order of the officers in the MVR, Ministry of Interior, it was necessary that the following people be given weapons and uniforms." That particular paragraph was shown to you yesterday by my learned colleague on pages 4793 through 4794 of the transcript. And you were asked, Ms. Groseva, about the information contained here. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At that time you indicated that you could not say where this particular data came from, because Mr. Krstevski had not been interviewed at the time that this document was generated by Mr. Ramicevic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can we please show marked for identification Exhibit P00485 [sic]. This may not be actually in e-court yet. Could we please with the usher's assistance, this is the document that we received, the Prosecution received recently. It was provided in hard copy on 10 September 2001. I apologise, Your Honours, we're just trying to locate the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe we could be of assistance, maybe we could provide our copies of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. We've actually found a hard copy. I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, you have the hard copy of this particular document in front of you in the Macedonian language. The -- again the English translation is currently, I believe, being uploaded and has been disclosed to the Defence but it was disclosed right before the court began today. Ms. Groseva, I would like to point it out, if we could, page 3 of this particular document. And if you could look at point 3 on page 3 of the Macedonian language, and if you take a look at that paragraph right underneath the first paragraph that is labelled with a 3. And that paragraph if I can read it says: "At this meeting it was emphasised that there is information on events that happened in Ljuboten village and it provides information that on 10 August 2001 about 20 persons came to police station Cair." And again this is, if you can look at the first page of this document, Ms. Groseva, this is the document pertaining to the information dated 28/5/2003, which you prepared. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this particular -- this particular document goes on to say: "These men, that is most of them, were known as perpetrators of crime acts. They asked for weapons and uniforms to be issued to them. After Ljube Krstevski, head of DOI Cair ordered no weapons or uniforms to be issued to these men, he gave that an explanation that there were no uniforms and weapons available in there. Then the next day, 11 August 2001, Ljube Krstevski informed the administrator of this police station by calling him on a mobile phone, that upon an order issued by senior officers of MOI, Ministry of Interior, he, the administrator should distribute weapons and uniforms to the following persons." Then it goes on to a list of names of persons. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Would you agree that the commission had not interviewed Mr. Krstevski at the time this particular information was produced?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, which information? The one on the screen or the one I have in front of me in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise, Ms. Groseva. We're talking about the one that you have in front of you. Is it true that the commission had not interviewed Mr. Krstevski according -- had not interviewed Mr. Krstevski at the time that the information you have in front of you in hard copy was produced?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this information indicates that we, as a committee, have received information or assertions with the facts that have you mentioned. To verify the accuracy of the assertions in the information as a document, if you continue further, you will see that the committee proposes that several persons are interviewed. So this is at the moment when the committee worked, this is an information received and the committee needs to verify the information. And therefore, among the persons to be invited is the head of the police station, Cair, Ljube Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So Mr. Krstevski had not been interviewed yet at the time that this information, the one that have you in hard copy in front of you, was produced?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he hadn't been.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is the information that we just went over in this particular paragraph on page 3 at point 3, is that information similar to the data contained in the document that we just read over prepared by Mr. Ramicevic?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it on the screen, but that -- that should be the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... So it's similar ... The information --

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You will be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance here in The Hague and for the assistance you have been able to give. You are, of course, now able to return to Macedonia, and the court officer will show you out. We thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you and I wish to thank you for your appreciation of my health condition, and I apologise if I have caused any inconvenience in the work of the Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, the Prosecution will call General Zoran Jovanovski. Your Honours, while we're waiting, I see that there is a document left on the witness table. Shall I remove it? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The transcript referred to the last document shown to the last witness as Exhibit 485. I'm told that should be Exhibit P435.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: General, would you please stand and read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: General, do you swear that the evidence you will give will be the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please -- Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, is your name General Zoran Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are you a citizen of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are you of Macedonian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the summer of 2001, what was your rank and position? Actually, I'm sorry, I went too quickly. General, when did you join the Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: February 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And in the summer of 2001, General, what was your rank and position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Until the month of May, I was a chief inspector in the posebna unit, and then after May, I was a deputy under-secretary, I was a deputy of the General Risto Galevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And -- and what was your rank at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say you were the deputy under-secretary under General Risto Galevski, does that mean you were the deputy under-secretary for the uniformed police department?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When were you promoted to general?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: That was in January/February 2002.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask the Prosecutor to use another microphone or to move closer to this one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... By the minister at the time, Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, General, my previous question was not translated or transcribed into the record so I'm going to ask you again. Who promoted you to the rank of general?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Boskoski, who at the time was the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. General, in the summer of 2003 [Realtime transcript read in error"2002"], did you continue to have the same position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document. Your Honours, we have some binders with some materials for you and also a copy for the witness and I think for the Defence. If we could ask the court usher to help us distribute them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this different from the bundle we received yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, there are some additional documents, Your Honour. In that sense, it is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not wish to interrupt but I think that the question of my learned friend, page 15, line 8, I think that he said -- asked that in the summer of 2003 and in the transcript it says 2002. So if I didn't hear well, I apologise. If I heard right, I would like to correct the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic heard quite well. I'm very grateful for catching it. It should say summer of 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you could turn, please, to what is tab 2 in the set of documents in front of you, and below the English version you'll find a Macedonian version. This -- I can perhaps assist the Court. This is from what has been marked for identification as Exhibit P379, or if it is simpler, this would also be found in Rule 65 ter 285.5. General, this is a document dated the 7th of March, 2003, and it is entitled, "Decision on the establishment of a commission." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to bother the court usher but could the General's left microphone, please be turned on. The General -- has solved the problem. Thank you very much. And part one of this decision says: "That a commission of inquiry into the circumstances and facts related to the events and incidents which took place in the territory of Ljuboten village, Skopje, in August 2001, is hereby established within the Ministry of the Interior consisting of the following members." And General, do you see your name there, the first person who is named there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Major-General Zoran Jovanovski. And if you look at the second part of this decision, we see that the commission shall have the task to investigate and analyse all materials and documents relating to the events which took place in the territory of Ljuboten, Skopje in this period. This is at page 2 of the English version and page 2 of the Macedonian version. "Including the identity of each of its members individually; establish the causes and circumstances surrounding the deaths of the victims; the material damage inflicted in order to establish the truth about the aforementioned events; investigate how the legal powers of the unit were exercised; and assess the consequences of the action." Have you been able to follow me, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, and we see that this decision to establish this commission was rendered by Hari Kostov, who was then the minister of the interior. General Jovanovski, after you received this decision issued by Minister Kostov to establish this commission, did you have any discussions with Minister Kostov about the work of the commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe what you wanted to discuss with Minister Kostov and how the discussion went.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: All of those listed here as members of this committee, they were all in managerial positions, and they certain tasks that they had to perform. In section 2 where these responsibilities are outlined considered for this committee which besides its regular tasks will not be in a situation to fully respond to the second part of the tasks. This is under number 2, Roman. The minister, I got a verbal approval that the committee should decide what is it a priority and what is it that can be completed within the time-frame given.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And was it after that discussion that the commission began its work? [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I couldn't say that we started working right away, because it was very difficult to get all of us together. We all had other responsibilities, other current responsibilities. However, we started working.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you another document, if I may. If you could turn, please, to what is tabbed as document 17, and this is Exhibit P00073, at tab 17. Actually, I'm sorry, I misspoke. Could you turn, please, to -- well, no. Stay with tab 17, please, which is P00073. We see here, General, that, that on the 13th of August, 2001, then Minister of Internal Affairs Ljube Boskoski issued a decision to establish a commission. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I only see the information here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn to tab 17? You seem to be on tab 19 -- 18 right now.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There you are. Do you see that decision there that was issued on the 13th of August --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, if can you turn, please, to tab 18, which is Exhibit P00378. Take a look at the Macedonian version, please, General. We see this document is titled, Report submitted to the ministry of the interior regarding an examination of the circumstances and an analysis of the activities undertaken by the security forces for the Ministry of Interior to repulse armed attacks by terrorist groups on the 12th of August, 2001, in the village of Ljuboten, Skopje. And then we see it is submitted by the commission formed by the resolution that was issued on the 13th of August. Do you see that on the first page?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then on the last page we see that this report was signed by the three members of the commission, Goran Mitevski, Risto Galevski, and Zivko Petrovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When, in 2003 when your commission --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In 2003, when the commission that you headed was doing its work, did it have this report available to it, the report that's in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall, did the commission that you led in 2003 have any other materials available to it that were produced by the commission that operated in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yeah. Did the commission that you led in 2003 have any other materials available to it that had been produced by the commission that did its work in 2001, the earlier commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, just the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. General, during the work of the commission in 2003, did any person or institution exert any pressure or influence on its work?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. There was no pressure by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, did the commission that you led speak with some of the persons who been involved or had allegedly been involved in the events in or around Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we interviewed several individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And amongst these individuals that your commission interviewed, were there interviews or discussions with members of the Ministry of Interior, with civilians, or both?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, both with employees from the ministry and with civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall, General, approximately how many times the committee that you led in 2003 met?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: About five or six times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, when the commission that you led spoke with persons, was any kind of coercion or threats or pressure put on those persons to make them give information to the commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. There was no pressure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I couldn't hear the last word that the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. The last word was commission, sorry. General, could a person having a discussion with the commission in 2003 refuse to answer questions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the commission keep records of its work and its discussions with persons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we kept the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who created these records or these minutes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Those were employees in the sector for analytics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you recall the name of one or more of them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Most of them were taken by Tanja Groseva. And the first one as we saw now, there was another person from her sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And tell us, please, how were these minutes created?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: The committee members and myself as the chair, we were asking questions of those that we had invited. The individuals would respond or comment on what they had to say, and the analytician [as interpreted] was writing down as much as she could in terms of minutes, wrote down those notes and in the end we produced a report that was then submitted to the members, and to the minister or to me as a chief of this working group of this committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go a little bit more slowly with you, General. You mentioned how the person from the analytical sector would take notes and at some point were these notes transformed into minutes or an information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: This was not regulated anywhere whether that was going to be a report or minutes. What was important that we came out with the document from a meeting that was held or with an interview with certain individuals, so the title of this document is not so important whether it is information or minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. The -- the document that was produced, would these documents have included 100 per cent of what the individual speaking with the commission had said?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe, then, or explain how much of the information was compiled in a document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: A maximum of 80 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And when these documents were compiled, did the members of the commission review them to see if they agreed with their accuracy before they were finalised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: The minutes or the information from the meeting that was held, or interview, as a rule, needs to be submitted to all members of the committee. Now whether they read those or not, I could not say. However, they're -- everybody receives a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you review these reports or minutes before they were finalised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In addition to these reports or minutes, or information, the documents that were produced, did some of the persons interviewed also produce handwritten reports or an Official Note about their participation in the events in or around Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the individuals took notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, some of the individuals were writing down things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And why was it important both to create reports or minutes and also to have the individual writing down in their own handwriting information related to these events? Why were both done?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: In some cases, some things need to be explained well, or maybe the person that is interviewed or interrogated cannot explain things well so that person handwrites these statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And what was done with these handwritten statements and then the typed up minutes or reports? What was done with all of this material eventually?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: They -- it was submitted to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All of this material?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, can you recall when the commission that you led met for the first time approximately, or the month?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I think it was May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If I could ask you, General, please, to turn to what is the third document in the materials in front of you. It should say tab 3. Do you see the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is from exhibit marked for identification P379 or 65 ter 285.24.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, do you see the report that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's dated the 6th of May --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's dated the 6th of May, 2003 -- I stand corrected if it should say information rather than report. About the meeting of the commission investigating the events in Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this information describes conversations with a number of individuals. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at the end we see that this information was submitted to the under-secretary of the police department. My question for you is this: Was this information or this record made following the same procedure that you described a couple of minutes ago? Notes were taken --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you and the other members of the committee have the opportunity to review this information before it was finalised and suggest changes or correct mistakes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I looked at it, reviewed it but I'm not sure about the others. I couldn't say that about the others because this was also submitted to the minister as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. But you reviewed before it was finalised for accuracy?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: That is correct. It is relative but it can be said that it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can turn now to what is the document at tab 10 in the materials in front of you, General. This is, again, from the same exhibit number, 65 ter 285.7. Do you see the document in the Macedonian version there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's dated 12 November 2003. And the first word in the English version of the title, it says minutes. I don't know if you would prefer to use the word information. But it's the minutes of a meeting of the commission for inquiry into the events and incidents in Ljuboten village. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it describes a discussion that the commission had with Mr. Johan Tarculovski. And then if you could please turn to -- actually, at the top of the first page, the first paragraph, it also indicates that Mr. Johan Tarculovski was present with his attorney. Do you see that in the very first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you turn to the second page now, you see two signatures. One of them over the name -- or under the name Johan Tarculovski; and another signature under the name Major-General Zoran Jovanovski, president of the commission. General, is that your signature there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was this document produced in the same manner that you've described to us before?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you also have the opportunity to review -- to review this document before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: As I can see two people, both people are signing so that means that both people were supposed to agree with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So then I -- can I take that response to mean both you and Mr. Tarculovski had the opportunity to review this document before it was signed? [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, to your knowledge, was any member of the police or the Ministry of Interior ever disciplined or punished in any way for their actions in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: As a deputy under-secretary at the time, I had no authority to discipline or reward any colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I understand that, General. I'm sorry, my question was something different. I'm simply asking about your knowledge. My question is: Do you have any knowledge or information that any member of the police or the Ministry of the Interior was ever disciplined or punished for their actions in or around Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think the witness is having a problem hearing the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's okay. It's good. If can you just repeat this, because the -- the interpretation was interrupted at one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sure. General, I'm simply asking about your knowledge. Do you have any knowledge or any information that any member of the Macedonian police or any member of the Ministry of the Interior was ever disciplined or punished for their activities in or around Ljuboten in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I know about the work of the police, at the end of each month there is analysis of the work of the police officers, and some police officers are disciplined, other police officers are rewarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that, General. But you still actually haven't answered my question. Do you want me to repeat the question again?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot say specifically about Ljuboten. I cannot say that somebody was disciplined because of Ljuboten or that a person was rewarded because of Ljuboten specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So I think, then, in answer to my question, you have no such knowledge then.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If you can turn, please, to what is at tab 11. Actually, let me go back for a moment, before you go to tab 11, General. You mentioned a moment ago that at the end of each month there's analysis of the work of police officers and some police officers are disciplined and other police officers are rewarded. Would that information as to who's being disciplined, who's being rewarded, commended, would that information be passed up to your office and your supervisor then, Risto Galevski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: That is by organisational units. Each organisational unit prepares a report for discipline and reward of its members.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And is that information then passed up the chain of command to the higher ranks of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: We can have an insight, but -- but I'm not sure if they're always sent up the chain of command. I have not encountered anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall, after August 2001, after the events in Ljuboten, receiving any information that any member of the police or the Ministry of Interior had been disciplined or rewarded, related to the events in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: The then head of SVR Skopje was returned to the Mr. Zoran Efremov was returned to his home town of Stip. I cannot recall about others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And that was some kind of a disciplinary matter, related to Mr. Efremov?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I'm not the person who can comment on decisions whether that is disciplinary or not. But the person was sent back from where he came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. But was that in relation to any activities that Mr. Efremov had conducted in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on. If you take a look, please, at what is tab 11. And this is, again, from what has been marked for identification as P00379, 65 ter 285.11. General, if you take a look, please, at the Macedonian version, you will see that this is a document dated the 20th of November, 2003. It is submitted by Staff-Sergeant Miodrag Stojanovski. It's an Official Note. It is one of the records supplied from the Macedonian government to the Office of the Prosecutor related to the work of your committee. And it says: "Subject, weapons issued to volunteers in 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says: "On the 25th of July 2001, a group from the Kometa agency led by Johan Tarculovski employed at the security sector of the R M MVR arrived at the police station OOV. They presented a list to commander Gjorgji Mitrov and asked to be issued with weapons as volunteer police reservists. The commander, having consulted his superiors at the security sector, ordered me to issue the weapons. Half of the men from the list were issued with weapons on 25 July 2001, and the other half on 26th July, 2001, after which they were sent to the CO KOB, security training centre to join other volunteers and fill out the questionnaires for police reservists." General, are you familiar with the place called PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That is a police station for securing objects and persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And to your knowledge, would it have been possible to arm a group of volunteer police reservists at this police station or at PSOLO without the knowledge of the minister in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. In 2001, were you familiar with a security agency in Macedonia called Kometa?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard about the security agency Kometa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall the name of the gentleman who was the head of the Kometa agency in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Unfortunately, he has the same name and last name as I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And does this gentleman have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, Bucuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Before we talk a little bit more about the agency known as Kometa, I want to go back for a moment where you told us that in 2001 it would have been possible to arm a group of volunteer police reservists at PSOLO without the knowledge of the minister. Would it have been possible to arm a group of volunteer police reservists without an order from someone in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: There's no special order given to issue weapons. There is a description of a procedure to give weapons to the persons. So any volunteer who wanted to be in the reserves at that moment could have been issued weapons without a specific order being issued and approval obtained from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, I wasn't -- again, I wasn't in this question referring to an order or approval from the minister. I'm saying -- my question is: Would the arming of a group of police reservists have at least required the order or the approval of someone in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I answered that the approval is obtained from the immediate superiors, while an order is received from, let’s say, the Minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So then approval for the arming of a group of volunteer reservists would come from the superior or superiors of the person who issue weapons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: There is no need for something like that. There is an instruction how fire-arms are issued. I'm not sure if you understood me. There is no need to obtain approval or special order, in order to issue weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. As long as the procedures are followed, the procedures of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: They need to be followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to what is tab 19 in your -- in your binder. This is 65 ter number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, before we take a look at this, can you recall whether your commission interviewed the man known as Bucuk in 2003?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And this is a document, if you take a look at the first page, it says up at top: "Persons issued with weapons on the 25th and 26th July 2001." And then it's the list or a table with the first column being a number, second column being last name and first name, then it says automatic rifle, automatic rifle ammunition, pistol, camouflage uniform, boots, et cetera. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we go to the very last page in both versions, you see that this -- there's a sentence at the bottom of the last page over the initials of Miodrag Stojanovski and it says: "I hereby confirm that I personally compiled this list pursuant to a list that the Kometa employees gave me before I started issuing them with weapons." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you could focus, please, on the first page in the Macedonian version of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for Your Honours and others following along in English, you might want to look at page 4 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But, General, in the Macedonian version on that first page, can you scroll down, look at those names and can you see any names on that list that you recognise as persons who worked for the Kometa security agency in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Only the owner Bucuk, not anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And is that the name you see at number 21, Zoran Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recognise any of the other names?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would ask that this document be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P436, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, during 2001, during the crisis period, and, General, maybe you could turn the right-hand microphone on that's in front of you. Do you see the green button? Thank you. During 2001, during the crisis time, General, did the Ministry of Interior engage members of the Kometa security agency for different tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it once again. Whether ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the Minister of the Interior engage or contract, employ members of the Kometa security agency for different tasks or jobs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Did -- to your knowledge, did members of the Kometa security agency participate in operations of the Macedonian security forces against the NLA?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. General, do you know if Johan Tarculovski and Ljube Boskoski knew each other in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I can't say whether they knew one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Since I have never seen them together anywhere, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. One question for you: In 2001, while General -- excuse me, while Ljube Boskoski was the minister of the interior, could Mr. Boskoski give orders to members of the army?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the spring and summer and autumn of 2001, how often would you speak with Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: As often as I need to speak in the line of the duty, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that. But could you be slightly more specific, even if it is just an approximation, once a day, once a week, several times a week, several times a day, or did it vary?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Once a week in the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And apart from that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Apart from that, no, I had another superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In 2001, before the events at Ljuboten, General, were there instances where members of the Macedonian police used some excessive force or committed some kind of misconduct? Can you recall any incidents of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I don't recall anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you recall whether Minister Boskoski placed an importance on maintaining discipline and order amongst the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: That was stressed as a priority at every meeting, to abide by the rules, by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if the witness could be given some more water, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, please just change my glass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder whether that is a convenient time, Mr. Saxon. You'd like to continue? Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If it's all right, it would just be one or two more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, when you say that was stressed as a priority at every meeting to abide by the rules and abide by the law, was that stressed by Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is where it came from, from the ministers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall what steps, if any, did Minister Boskoski take to ensure that good discipline and order was maintained amongst the police. Give some examples.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the police department there was a sector for public law and order where there were seven or eight inspectors who were in the field on a daily basis and they would control the proper operation in the police stations, sectors, or departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that. But the question that I asked you was specifically related to Minister Boskoski. Do you want me to repeat my question again?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall, General, what steps, if any, did Minister Boskoski take to ensure that good discipline and order was maintained amongst the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: The minister himself, his duty is to ensure that the inspectors who are employed in the ministry enforce the ministry's policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And during that -- during 2001, during, for example, the meetings of the collegium, did you see or hear Minister Boskoski take steps to ensure that those inspectors were doing their job?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can't understand you. The minister is not the manager of those inspectors. The minister is managing the higher -- highest rank in the ministry, because our ministry has a hierarchy. We have general police that controls the police. We have the head of the crime police who is in charge of the order among his ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I guess maybe -- let me ask my question a different way, General. You explained that the duty, one of the duties of the minister is to ensure that the inspectors who are employed in the ministry enforce the ministry's policy regarding discipline. And I'm just asking you whether you can recall seeing or hearing Minister Boskoski take any particular steps, give any particular orders to make sure that those inspectors were doing their job properly, that's all.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Specific orders, he could not give to the -- to the inspectors. He could give orders to his direct associates such as the director, the director would then forward the orders to the under-secretaries. He often visited the sectors for internal affairs where he would hold meetings with the heads of stations and he would then receive information on how the law is enforced and how the operation went.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And interpreter's correction in line 36.10, police general instead of general police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you say that Minister Boskoski would often visit the sectors for internal affairs and hold meeting with the heads of stations and receive information on how the law was enforced and how an operation went. Did you ever accompany the minister on such visits?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I apologise, I did not say operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's how it was translated into English. The English transcript said, The minister would often visit sectors for internal affairs where he would hold meetings with the heads of stations and he would then receive information on how the law is enforced and then in English it says and how the operation went. Would you like to correct the end of that sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter could offer clarification, operation in the sense of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Oh. Did you ever accompany the minister in such --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no operations mentioned in my work is the witness's answer. If I was invited, I would accompany him, but it has happened once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And when the minister would receive information on those visits would the minister ever issue instructions or orders based on the information that he received?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. At the collegium, so every Monday when is there a collegium, the weekly work is summarized and new tasks are issued for the week that follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we can stop there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 20 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to inform the Chamber that today and the following days of this week, the attorney Nikola Kunovski who is a member of the Defence team for Mr. Boskoski will also attend the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Jovanovski, before we took the break you had explained that sometimes the minister would go visit other ministries, sectors or police stations and speak with commanders, get information, and then at the weekly collegium meetings the minister might issue -- assign tasks based on that information. Can you give some examples of the kind of tasks or the kinds of instructions that the minister would give at the collegium meetings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: They were primarily related to - how should I say? - construction works, improvement of the working conditions, then if some uniform parts are missing, then they should be procured, that the police officers should look properly, then if there are some comments regarding the outlook of the building, then the minister would issue recommendations; so this is all related to the daily work, not something in the extreme.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So the minister issued tasks related to the daily work of the Ministry of the Interior. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned the subject that police officers should look properly. And what do you mean by that? What -- what do you mean by "police officer who looks proper"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: To have the proper hat, proper neat uniform, shirt, trousers, shoes, the belt and the equipment they carry should also be neat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why is that important that police officers wear uniform? Why is that important?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm now speaking about the police officers who are wearing the uniform on a daily basis. I'm not speaking about everyone employed in the ministry. Not everyone is wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, General, I understand that. I'm talking about members of the police who wear uniforms. My question is simply why is that important that -- that uniformed policemen wear a uniform? What is the significance of the uniform?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: The uniform has several aspects of significance. One is it works as a prevention. Those who are planning to commit a offence when they see a police officer they will be deterred from committing a crime or a misdemeanour. Then we are of assistance for the citizens. And to maintain public law and order, to prevent it from disturbances.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does the uniform, then, assist both police officers, criminals and the public in identifying who is a policeman and who is not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Back in 2001, were you aware of any instances where persons were wearing police uniforms and carrying fire-arms but were not police officers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: There are several types of police officers. I don't know which of those you are referring at. If you are referring to the blue, the regular uniform, there were no such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. General, in late May 2001, were you seriously injured in a NLA mortar attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Following that attack, can you recall what other units, if any, were created in the Ministry of Interior to protect Macedonia from the threat of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: During that period, apart from the regular police, we had a provisional unit that was established but it was activated temporarily, the posebna unit, and the unit for special tasks, Tiger.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were any other units or groups of police officers set up during the spring or summer of 2001 that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Not in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. General, can you recall that in June 2001 there was fighting between the Macedonian security forces and the NLA at the town of Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall that after the NLA was pulled out of Aracinovo there were large demonstrations in the centre of Skopje by persons who were upset with the actions of the government?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: There were unrests in the centre of the city, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you present in Skopje on the evening when those demonstrations occurred?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, in Skopje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you observe part or all of these demonstrations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters wish to note that there appears to be interference between both microphones of the Prosecutor which are on. So if you could move closer to one of them, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, on Friday, 10th of August, 2001, eight Macedonian soldiers were killed when a mine exploded at Ljubotenski Bacila. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you learn about this event; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall whether you informed Minister Boskoski about this event?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. I haven't informed him myself, not me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have an opportunity to observe any reaction of Minister Boskoski related to the news about the incident at Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall any discussions within the ministry about this explosion at Ljubotenski Bacila and the death of the eight soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can't recall. Since my duties were outside of the ministry, I was not within the ministry during this period, so I don't know about the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You say your duties were outside of the ministry, but you were the under-secretary at the time -- excuse me, you were the deputy under-secretary at the time, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: After May, yes. But I'm referring to the headquarters of the ministry, so at the seat of the ministry I'm speaking about the facilities, the buildings where the Ministry -- employees of the Ministry of Interior are working. My tasks were outside of that courtyard where those buildings are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall what your tasks were on the 10th and 11th, and 12th of August, 2001, where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I made the daily rounds of the police officers who are at the check-points, for instance, or who were performing the daily duties. And regarding the 12th, I believe I was at my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say you made daily rounds of the police officers who were at the check-points, would those check-points have included check-points in the Ljuboten area, Ljubanci, Radisani?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I would say that there were other colleagues in charge of the Skopje region, or Skopje vicinity. I was making rounds of the Tetovo and Kumanov regions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. General, I would like to show you a video, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is from Rule 65 ter 988, and it's time code 133 -- I think I may be confusing my good case manager. Are we okay? It is time code 1 hour, 33 minutes and 18 seconds to 1 hour 35 minutes and 33 seconds. And it shows -- you'll see it will show -- Your Honour, my case manager has explained to me that this exhibit has been admitted -- excuse me, that this video has been admitted as exhibit 278. If we could call up that exhibit, please. And this is a video of a visit by Minister Boskoski to a police training base, I believe, if I'm pronouncing it correctly, the town called Penus on the 8th of November, 2001. I was wrong about the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop the tape, please. This is not the video-clip that I need to show. I need to show the video-clip from 65 ter 988, and it's time code 1:33:18. Do I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could stop the tape, Your Honour. Apparently, I have made an error somehow in designating which video-clip. So I'm going to withdraw my questions about this at this time. And at this time, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. And until I organise my things, I would also ask for the assistance of the usher to distribute some of the materials that I intend to use in the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the Prosecutor to switch off his microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I begin?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General Jovanovski.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, appear on behalf of Mr. Ljube Boskoski. General, before I start asking you questions, I will ask you, as I usually do, to listen to a caution that I wish to issue to you. I suppose that you understand the language I am speaking and I understand the language that you are speaking. However, my question and your answer need to be interpreted so that the Chamber and the colleagues in the courtroom are able to follow our exchange and this would be the way for us to be of best assistance to the Chamber. Therefore, I ask you to wait for my question to be interpreted and answer only then. Have you understood this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When asked by my learned colleague the Prosecutor, you stated that you were a police general in the police of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that you were employed in the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, and you're still employed there since 1986. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You graduated from the police academy at Skopje in 1989. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You worked for five years as regular police officer at Centar police station in Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until 1999, you were a member of the special unit Tiger. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1999, until May of 2001, you were at the duty of chief inspector of the posebna unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you told my learned colleague, in May you were appointed deputy under-secretary for the police department in the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In February 2002, you were appointed under-secretary for police in the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stayed at that office until May 2003, when you were appointed deputy 2 director of the public security bureau. Is that information correct as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Assistant to the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Considering the duties and the rank you had and you have in the Ministry of Interior, I will ask you to answer several questions, and the questions are related also to the questions asked of you by my learned colleague the Prosecutor. The first thing I wish to ask you is whether it is correct that the Ministry of Interior performs its duties and competences pursuant to the Law on the Ministry of the Interior and other legislation setting forth the tasks for the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the specific officers in the Ministry of the Interior performed their tasks pursuant to the Rule Book on the Organisation and Operation of the Ministry of Interior, that are setting forth precisely their duties and tasks. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Any job has a job description, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you would agree with me, although the Law on Internal Affairs establishes who are the authorised officer in the sense of that Law enumerates all the officers who could perform tasks within the realm of internal affairs who could use certain instruments, not every employee of the Ministry of Interior could perform just any task. One can perform only the tasks that are set forth in the general act of the ministry, the Rule Book on the Organisation and Operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if there were other witnesses testifying about this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, although there were other witnesses testifying about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want you to confirm that the Ministry of the Interior consisted of the public security and security administration and counter-intelligence as the state security, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And each of these parts of the ministry was headed by a director?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering questions by my learned colleague you stated that you were in the uniformed police department, and my question is: Is it correct that the uniformed police department is part of the -- of the sector for public security where there is also police forensics, crime police, analytics sector and other forms and sectors dealing with the activities of the internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The task of the uniformed police where you have spent your entire career, if we interpreted your statement correctly, so can I say that the uniformed police has -- has the primary importance for the maintaining of public law and order, while the crime police had the main task of working on detection of crimes, apprehension of perpetrates or prevention of crimes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also answered that in August or during the summer of 2001, your direct superior was General Risto Galevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
