utterances.text: And the public security bureau, as a whole, was, at that time, chaired by General Goran Mitevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you immediately, could you please answer what sort of professionals or professional standing enjoy Risto Galevski and Goran Mitevski your direct superiors. Could you please tell us your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: It was a honour for me to work with them. They were excellent professionals and they were very good superior officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that both the director of public security and the director of the state security are elected by the government and not the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. They are government officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And above --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, and the state security bureau is controlled by the parliament as well and not only the government of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the parliament there is a committee called parliamentary committee monitoring the work of this directorate and that committee exists to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering the questions of my learned colleague the Prosecutor, you mentioned the collegium of the minister. I would like to ask you to look at this document that is in tab 1, number 1, that is Exhibit 1D107, the page is 1D4371, that is the first page of the Macedonian version, while the first page in the English version is 1D4392. Do you recognise, General, this Rule Book on the Organisation and Operation of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is that the general act or the rule book that establishes in precise detail the tasks and the competences of the parts of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to turn to page 17, that is 1D4388 in the Macedonian language, and the English version is Article 26 at page 1D4412. I will ask to you look at this Article 26 now. And with regards to your answer, that usually you would attend once a week this collegium of the minister, is it correct that that collegium is regulated by this rule book and it establishes the composition of the collegium as well as the possibility that an extended composition is also in attendance at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to paragraph 2 of this Article, one can see that the minister, the deputy to the minister, the director of the public safety bureau, the director of the security and counter-intelligence directorate, heads of the police department, departments, head of the crime police department and the state secretary are in attendance while the paragraph 3 reads that apart from these mandatory members, also the heads of the sectors could participate, and, if needed, also other employees could participate in the collegium. So my question is now: Considering that since February 2002 you were under-secretary for police, you were one of those collegium members whose presence was mandatory at the sessions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we can understand that from that moment onwards, you were always attending the meetings of the collegium, of course, when you were in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And before that, in 2001, you would also be invited as one of those individuals who would be invited to the meetings pursuant to this Article of the rule book, depending on the issue reviewed at the meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You could have also attended at those times -- you could -- or you were present at that time when General Galevski was not present in Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: As his deputy, that's my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to this, from your personal experience, you could have spoken about the manner in which the Minister Boskoski managed the ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood well, he issued orders -- he issued orders to you, as you, then, to those immediately subordinate to him and the members of the collegium, and, in that manner, respected the chain of command that existed before him in the Ministry of Interior and which had been fully respected at his time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you now -- I would like to ask you the following. Would you agree with me if I said that Minister Boskoski fully respected the expert opinions and suggestions and recommendations of his directors, his under-secretaries regarding the issues about which they had the responsibility to inform him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that he respected the professional background of those people, of his people and at no moment did he look at his associates taking in account their national or political affiliation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: That was not a great virtue of his, but he always asked us to have the last word on a matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that during all times that he was the minister, his deputy was Refet Elmazi, an Albanian, that he was always present at the sessions and that the minister respected his opinion that he presented at the collegium sessions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: At the collegium, there were no differences between Albanians and Macedonians. We only took in account the functions and the positions, under-secretary, head of a department and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you: Did you belong to a political party in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not belong to any political party then, and I don't belong to a political party now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before Mr. Boskoski became the minister, you said that you were the chief inspector in the posebna. After that, during the time of Mr. Boskoski, you were appointed at the position of deputy under-secretary for the uniformed police. And after that, in February 2002, were appointed at the position of an under-secretary. Would you agree with me that Minister Boskoski, by appointing you at such a responsible position or positions within the ministry, most of all had a respect of your professional expert and ethical characteristics in the course of performing your work and he could not care less whether you belonged to a political party, especially not the political party to which he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the case it is with you, would agree that the Minister Boskoski kept the whole professional structure that he inherited when he took the position of a minister, or were only some of them reassigned to a different as important or even more important positions as a result of the change in the government?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: During the time of the Minister Boskoski, there was no significant reassignment of the professional -- of the expert -- of the experts as the case had been before him or since him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you say that at those positions of the ministry as high officials, even before Mr. Boskoski came to be a minister, both Ristovski [as interpreted] and Galevski, other managers of the sectors and the units?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, these names might not have been correct. We will provide with you a correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Galevski was deputy, he became under-secretary and Mitevski became deputy in the state security and then he came to the position in public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to finish up this question with you. Is it correct that after the elections in September of 2002 when there was a new government in power that at that moment many people were replaced from the ministry although in some cases those were exceptional professionals?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There is a statistics. I'm not exactly how much but I think it was over 50 per cent of the people that were replaced.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Therefore, looking at the Rule Book of the Organisation and Work of the Ministry of Interior, then you would agree with me that it is this rule book that determined who is performing the basic activities within the Ministry of Interior, and what are the -- what are the tasks that the minister performs himself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It has been determined that the vast majority of the work within the Ministry of Interior is being done in the sectors of the Ministry of Interior and in the units of the Ministry of Interior in the municipalities and only some activities are done on a republic level, that is, in the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia on a republic level. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The strategic documents and materials are prepared in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were answering the questions of my learned friend the Prosecutor about the issuing of weapons, you said that there was a rule book that regulated the manner in which weapons were issued at the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that the rule book's instructions or directives as general acts were those documents passed by the minister and through which he actually managed the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regardless whether these acts were passed by one of the previous ministers or the Minister Boskoski, those acts made all the employees working at those positions as they bound you as a manager in this position. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you -- the English page is 1D444, and the Macedonian page is 1D4390.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the English page was 1D4414.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, General, is it correct that always, together with the Rule Book on Organisation and Work, that this guidebook was accompanied by an accompanying document, a form, outlining the chain of command, and as the rule book changed, this chart was also changed as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, we look at the rule book that is entered into evidence and which -- on the 16th of June 2002 was passed by the minister of interior Dosta Dimovska. Please tell me: Is this rule book in force? The date was wrong. 26th of January, is the correct, 2001. In the course of the year, there were only small -- there were only some changes and addendums to this rule book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at this chart that is in front of you at the moment, is this chart in according -- according to the rule book in the first half of 2001, it indicates that for the minister of those units that were uniformed, only the special unit Tiger was directly reporting to the minister.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All other units of the police, the criminalistic police, had their own chain of command within the public security bureau. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that until May you were the chief inspector in the posebna. Therefore, posebna, as the chart indicates, was in the sector for the police department.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask you to look at document which is right after the tab 3, which -- Exhibit 1D66, and the page is 1D2321, the Macedonian, and the English one is 1D2407. General, in front of you, you can see the proposal for the changes of the organisation of the work of the Ministry of Interior from August 2001. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask to you turn to page 1D -- the numbers with the Macedonian is 1D2322, and the English one is 1D408.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the English version is 1D2408.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2408.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, in front you, you have the rule book for the changes of the Rule Book of the Organisation and the Work of the Ministry of Interior passed by the minister Ljube Boskoski. Is this manner of passing a rule book for the changes of a previously passed rule books a manner in which the minister by changing the general acts performed certain changes in the structure of the ministry and, in fact, continued to manage with the ministry by passing general acts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would these changes, in Article 1, stipulates that as it says here, in the third line from -- below the third line from below, that from August 1st, 2001, Article 1, the unit -- the special tasks unit Tiger, from the Article 7 is moved to the part A, department for police, in Article 4 and it becomes item 6?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct, General, if I say, that practically from August 1st, 2001, the only unit of uniformed police which was directly reporting to the minister, the special unit Tiger, it was transferred in the department of police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, look at the next page of the same document, 1D82323, the English one is 1D2409. As you have explained to us a little bit earlier together with the rule book and changes and addendums there is also a chart, the organisational chart, and tell me whether this chart clearly shows that the unit -- that the special tasks unit Tiger is in the department for police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In the last box, special task unit, Tiger.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, maybe this was a mistake or maybe this was a question to your colleague, therefore, I will leave this question for the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned in the second part on the structure of the Ministry of the Interior was the administration for security and counter-intelligence. And if I would say -- I would say that their task was to gather information and counter the work of foreign intelligence services, their centres and agents, then to protect the constitution, to counter terrorists and other activities that jeopardized the order in the country, et cetera. Is my understanding of the general tasks of the state security correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Globally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that besides certain methods used by the public security, the state security uses additional methods, has its own intelligence network in the country, among the enemy lines, abroad, it relies on information that it receives from other sources, of operative technology and so on. Is this all that the administration for security and public -- counter-intelligence does?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The way this administration works is very different from the work of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you have mentioned a little bit earlier that the minister relied on the professional opinions and recommendations of your colleagues and who were his associates, did this -- does this -- is this -- does this hold true both for the public security and the state security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information that you as experts from the police submitted to the minister [indiscernible], that was Minister Boskoski or other minister that this was a reliable information and there was no need that the minister to check the -- and corroborate the information that he received from you nor did the minister actually do this in practice?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Correct, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also asked about the manner in which the minister reacted after he would find out about some issues from his immediate subordinates. You gave several examples in the manner in which the minister managed with the collegium and issued instructions about the manners in which the -- it is ensured that the ministry performs its tasks prescribed by the law. You mentioned that within the ministry there was a department for inspection whose task was to check whether the bodies of the ministry work according to the law. Did I understand this well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the unit for professional standards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In a case -- in the case that a manager of this unit for professional standards or one of you, his associates or somebody outside of the ministry points out to some failures to do something, or an abuse of authority of the police, my question is: Did the minister undertake any other measures within his authority; for example, asking to set up a committee to investigate an issue that had reached the minister, or requested from you, from officials with authority, to shine a light on a certain situation, to be informed whether certain perpetrators or initiators of an activity, et cetera, et cetera, was this also a manner through which the minister attempted to learn some information, or suggest to you who the professionals working at the ministry, how to react?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever selected for a committee that had the task to investigate a certain problem?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Maybe not during his time, but later, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. We will return to these questions a little bit later. Since you already told us about the uniformed police and probably hear more about this in the future, and I would like to talk to you about this now, would it be correct to say that the realistic and true control over the work of the police officers that maintain public law and order is done by the commanders of the police stations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where my learned friend asked you about the weapons that were issued in the police station PSOLO, would you agree with me that the person responsible for the control of how the instructions for the issuing of the weapons is the commander of that police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: According to the act for the organisational chart, for each job position there is a responsibility and according to this act every commander is responsible for the work of his own police station, both for the equipment, for the facility and for everything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, there was no need for you who were in the immediate chain of command, it was not necessary for you to issue certain tasks or instructions to the commander of the police station, because it is his task, according to the rule book, all these things were clear to the commander of the police station what are his tasks and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe this is a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, before the break, you recall us saying that the police station commander is actually the officer issuing task and managing the police in the performance of its tasks. Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, also, that the police station commander as the direct superior of the uniformed police is the individual who, pursuant to the collective agreement of the Ministry of the Interior, gathers information and facts and makes proposals to instigate disciplinary procedure if some of the police officers or someone from among the police officers in the police station has been involved in a disciplinary offence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Disciplinary offence is regulated precisely with the collective agreement and the responsibility of the officers could not be ascertained in a different way, only through the procedure that is prescribed by the collective agreement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister only establishes the disciplinary committee which is a standing committee with a permanent composition and has a longer period of -- of term of office, and that committee carries out the procedure that is prescribed by the collective agreement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. And there is a member of the trade union in the committee. The trade union representative represents the interests of the employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that committee produces a proposal to the minister and the minister could accept or reject the proposal made by the committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the minister himself could not make a proposal and could not sanction the employee without the procedure or outside the procedure that would be following the rules in the collective agreement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We also spoke a while ago about the notion that the minister, in order to receive more detailed information about an event or about an issue, could establish a committee, or a working group, task force. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That right of the minister and of other senior officers is established in the rule book and in the law. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And those committees could be of permanent composition such as a disciplinary committee but could also be ad hoc committees established for a certain purpose or for a shorter period of time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, General, to look at this second part in Roman numeral II, that is tab 5. This is Exhibit 1D112, and the page is 1D4304, while the English is 1D4306. Is it correct, General, that at the beginning of the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia there was a need for the facts related to the crisis to be gathered, compiled so that the competent bodies of the ministry could be informed and react to a given situation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have in front of you the act, the decision to establish the headquarters of the operative action Ramno that the committee -- that was the headquarters that was established on the 7th of March, 2001 by the then minister Dosta Dimovska. You can see that on the second page of the document. And do you agree with me that this headquarters of Ramno comprised the most responsible officers in the line of command in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look in tab 6, 65 ter 1D476, that is Macedonian page is 1D0 -- 1D4300, while the English page is 1D4302.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please. The microphone appears to be out of order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I gave you the page numbers, so you have now in front of you the decision dated 29th of May, 2001, and on the second page of the decision you can see that this decision was passed by the minister, Ljube Boskoski. The second page of the decision is 1D4301, and the English is 1D4303. General, you can see from the composition of these headquarters that the Minister Boskoski respecting the changes at the most senior positions in the bureaus for public and for the state security and in the police department appointed new composition of the headquarters, Ramno. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you then became member of the headquarters Ramno. Your name is number 4. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we can now go back to the first page, because we are now discussing the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as can you see from both these decisions, the first and the second one, the Minister Boskoski was not among the members, neither in the headquarters Ramno that the minister Dimovska established nor in the headquarters that he himself established. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that the headquarters Ramno received information from the sectors and from the departments for internal affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, information of relevance for the assessment of the state of crisis?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And -- and it received information from both the public and the state security directorates.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For you, the members of the headquarters, the office of the headquarters Ramno produced information, documents containing those relevant information, important information about the events, the territory of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, every morning we received a bulletin presenting information about the events at the territory of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the headquarters, Ramno, so you, who were appointed members of the headquarters Ramno, informed the minister only about the most important information from among those that you received. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So would you agree with me if I say that the information arriving from the units for internal affairs in the municipalities and from the sectors never went to the minister directly. They went to the headquarters Ramno and the minister was informed only about the most important issues necessary for him to be able to perform his duties as a minister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This same decision, item 8, reads that there is a member from the analytics department who gathered all the information that arrived to us and compiled that information document about the most important developments, and that information was forward to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And since you have just mentioned this, that was the practice and that was the customary way of operation in the Ministry of the Interior in every committee, in any working body, there would always be someone from the analytics department, and the analytics department was the one to forward the information produced by that -- that body or that committee to the minister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that this decision about the establishment of the headquarters Ramno of 29th of May, 2001 is received as Defence exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the Prosecution's understanding that this document has already been admitted and it has the number P00381.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that is correct, I would like to thank my colleague and then there is no need for this decision to be received in evidence again. We will now verify this once again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you a while ago whether you have ever been a member of some groups or committees, and we were just reminded that you have been a member of the headquarters Ramno. I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 7, and that is Exhibit 1D113. That is 1D4312, the Macedonian page, while 1D4314 is the English page. You have in front of you the decision of the Ministry of Interior of 18th of June, 2001, by which the minister of the interior passes a decision to establish a committee to investigate whether the complaints of the members of the Albanian community in the Republic of Macedonia related to abuse of powers by the members of the police -- of the ministry of the internal affairs were well-founded. This decision probably reminded you that this committee existed and that you were the president of this committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you the following question, General. If we look at the composition of this committee, after your name, Zoran Jovanovski, there is the name Emini Ismet. Emini Ismet is an officer of the Ministry of the Interior who is of Albanian nationality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My first question is, is it correct that throughout the crisis all your colleagues, Albanians, in the Ministry of Interior still remained at their offices and together with you tried to resolve the crisis situation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction 68/8, ethnicity instead of nationality.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the second page of this document, 1D4313, and the English page is 4317 -- I apologise. 4314 and continues to 4315. The tasks are established and the item 2 says that the committee has the task to establish whether the allegations and the complaints, individual and group complaints submitted to the Ministry of Interior by the ethnic Albanian citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, as well as non-governmental organisations and relating to claims that certain members of the ministry have abused powers of their office in the performance of their tasks, whether those allegations were well-founded. Do you remember that this was the task for the committee?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that the first thing that this committee did was to publically through the media address all citizens so that they report any case of abuse of powers by the members of the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. There was a public ad through the media so regarding any abuse of office. Not only excessive use of force or ill-treatment but rather any illegal conduct of the Ministry of the Interior should be complained, that they should explain to the Ministry of the Interior or to the regional organisational unit of the ministry and those complaints were then forwarded to us, the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, is it also correct that you never received a specific complaint regarding specific event or against a specific person, rather, all complaints spoke generally about the abuses of the police powers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Specifically had there been any kind of a report to -- there was no report made to our committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this the reason because of which you, General, organised a meeting with the Albanian intellectuals in Skopje so you can discuss with them and find out the reasons for which the Albanian population does not wish to report specific cases although in the public there were rumours that those things were actually happening?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the spirit of the proper working of the Ministry of Interior, we, as a working group established -- we initiated meetings with intellectuals, so to speak, but most of them were young people, young Albanians with whom we discussed so they could convince their neighbours to report all the improper working of the members of the Ministry of Interior, and that they should report these incidents to the Ministry of Interior or to the regional office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in spite of these efforts undertaken by you, that you did not get specific names and that it was impossible for the responsible bodies of the ministry to propose the investigation according to their authority?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that because of this you suggested that working together with the OSCE undertake a number of preventative measures in order to prevent such cases or stop them from happening, that the minister accepted these suggestions, and that subsequently at all police stations and at all check-points instructions were sent outlining how they should behave towards the people, or what -- what civil rights the police should protect during their interaction with the people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: During this time in 2001, the OSCE was very active and working together with them, we prepared the material which was then distributed to all organisational units of the Ministry of Interior, which, in turn, had the tasks to disseminate among the population. And in this -- these document said that all individuals who are detained for any reason should be aware of their rights and responsibilities with respect to the Ministry of Interior, that they have the right call a lawyer, that they have a right to make a phone call, and they have the right to -- I cannot now remember exactly what their rights were, but all their -- all the rights that a person has were outlined there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend the Prosecutor asked you about the events that transpired on 25th of June in Skopje. Is it correct that the police - and at that time you were the second person in the police in the Republic of Macedonia - that in the course of such situations where the public law and order were seriously infringed upon to protect those and secure those parts of the city were populated by Albanians in order to prevent the mob to cause any damage to the Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: If we speak about this critical date, we were defending the parliament where there was a huge crowd gathered around, and we also had police forces in those parts where Albanians and Macedonians lived together, and in order to avoid mass fights or mass problems with the law and order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were probably aware that those responsible in -- that citizens in those parts, in Skopje, Bitola, or in all the cities where there were major problems with the public law and order in the cities where there was a damage caused of the property of the Albanians or in those places where their security was jeopardized, then in those situations there was a request that the -- that the -- that the bodies that had the authority within the Ministry of Interior should undertake all the necessary measures in order to find the perpetrators and -- so they can be punished.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I know, over 80 percent of such events were clarified, were -- were finalised and there was a criminal report initiated against the perpetrators of the Macedonian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I remind you that only the department -- the security department in Bitola initiated over 100 criminal reports and in Skopje there were a number of criminal misdemeanour reports, then would you agree with me that my information is correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly what I had in mind. I did not know the exact number but I would say that in percentages that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at the document after the tab 8, which is Exhibit 1D114. 1D4316 in Macedonian, and 1D4318 in the English. Can you also see this one decision of the Minister Boskoski on the 26th of June of 2001, this is the reaction of the minister, in order to determine what had happened and the reasons for which this huge demonstrations of the citizens, the police and the army took place between the 25th and the 26th of June, 2001. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, is it true that we met briefly yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During our meetings I showed you certain documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask you to look at the document after the tab 9; this is Exhibit 1D115. That is exhibit -- that is 1D4328. 1D4328, and the Macedonian page is 1D4326.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpetation] The Macedonian 1D4328, and the English one, 1D4330.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the decision for establishing a working group for the -- from May 28th, 2001. And on the second page, we can see that this was also a decision made by the minister, Ljube Boskoski. Please, I would like you to look at -- I would like to ask you to look at the document past tab 10. It is Exhibit 1D116. The page is 1D4324 in the Macedonian, and 1D4325 -- no, it is 1D4326 is in English. You remember that I showed you these documents.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said in 2001 you did not -- you were not aware that there was a work group established for the purpose of collecting evidence for potential war crimes that were perpetrated on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia but that you, later on, when there was a change in the government, you heard from some members of the committee who addressed the public that the new government destroyed the documents that they had collected. Do you remember telling me that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that did not deal with this issue because you were dealing with issues of the uniformed police and you only noticed and stated that there was such a discussion in the public. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you will probably agree with me, General, that during this crisis time it was very important that a minister establishes a group of people who would deal with the issue of investigating all events that would -- that would constitute a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Earlier you have stated that in 2001 there was a special unit, Tiger. Do you remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A number of people testified about the special unit Tiger in front of this Chamber. I will not ask you questions about the statements made by these people who testified. Since you were a member of the Tigers until 1999, you knew that the special unit Tiger existed much earlier, much before Mr. Boskoski became the minister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: I remember from 1986. I think it might have been in existence since 1983.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Until the battalion for rapid intervention within the ministry, that was the only special unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A little bit earlier in the chart we noticed that this unit, until the August 1st was directly reporting to the minister, and after that was transferred to the department for police.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the types of work that you did, could you tell me whether you are aware that on the 10th and 11th August in Radishan, there was a major attack of the NLA at the police station and the security forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding the -- considering the types of work that you were doing, could I remind you that the Tiger unit was involved in these fights?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it was involved in the activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that your under-secretary Risto Galevski was at Radusa together with the unit Tiger?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind military activities and responsibilities of the Tiger unit that they had in Radusa, would you testify in front of this Court that Tiger could not have been at Ljuboten on August 12th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to you look at document beyond tab 3. Actually, the Roman III; the tab is number 14. That is Exhibit 1D108. This is a single-page document so I don't need to state the page numbers. This is a memo that was sent on the 5th of May, 2003 to the department for police. That is actually the department where you were the under-secretary at that time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This was sent after we had received the decision to investigate the Ljuboten events, and it was sent to all units who has to answer who has deployed forces where on that critical date, and this is a response to this request of ours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And from this information, you can see that it was sent by the commander of the special unit, Goran Zdravkovski and that it went through regular channels as the communication in the ministry goes normally. So it was sent to you in the police department, and it was not sent to the committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to this, considering what you have stated now and considering what you have known then in August 2001, are the contents of this information accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at document in tab 15. That is it Exhibit 1D56. This is, again, a single-page document. This is a document that was also sent to the police department on the 7th of November, 2001, by the commander of the special task force Tigers, Toni Stankovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We requested once again information from this unit because in the previous information it was written until only the 12th and it was nothing written there about the 13th; so we asked the commander to clarify once again where was the unit deployed during those critical dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And considering your duties in August 2001, could you testify that the contents of this information are accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, answering the questions of my learned colleague, you also stated that for a while you were also working in the posebna unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And several people have testified about that unit before this Court already, so I will ask you only about some issues, so maybe some issues that remained open so that they are clarified. You stated that you were the chief inspector of the posebna unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of the east posebna unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That title, chief inspector, is required for a person to be the commander of the posebna unit.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: The act on the establishment of the posebna unit reads that the head of the posebna unit is the head in the rank of chief, while the three units are headed by chief inspectors. So the job in the Ministry of Interior is systematized as in the organisational structure as chief inspector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the decision about the posebna unit specifies which is the level that should be met or possessed by someone in the Ministry of the Interior, in order to be a battalion commander, and which is the level for a person to be the head of all three battalions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this was also established in the rule book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. A person needs to have university education, certain numbers of years of service in that area, to -- for both the police chief or the head of department or chief inspector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at this document in tab 5, and the white tab is 27. And that is Exhibit 1D62. The page is 1D2357, while the English page is 1D2364. As you explained earlier, the rule books are amended through amendments of the rule books, while here you have in front of you the rules amending the rules on systemization of jobs in the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the page 2 of this document. That is 1D2358 in Macedonian, and 1D2365 in English. And the Article 1, at the end, before this table starts, specifies that these amendments are amending the previous rule books that are enumerated in the Article 1, the most recent is the one of the 28th of August, 2001. And the Article 2 is amended in the public security bureau in part I, police department, item 5, sector for special units is hereby amended and now reads. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now we have in the table, first, under the number 5, sector for special units, and below that we have what you have seen -- what you spoke about, what are the qualifications for each of the heads necessary for them to perform the task in the posebna unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was stipulated in this way in all previous rule books that were enumerated in Article 1 here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please turn to the second page. That is 1D2359, Macedonian, and 1D2366, English. And in the upper part, you have 5.1, rapid interventions battalion-Lions with the overall structure and the conditions that or prerequisites that those persons need to meet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you now that the amendments to the rule book were introduced in order to establish this rapid interventions battalion, then this would be correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this amendment to the rule does not change anything about the posebna units.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it doesn't change anything. It only amends.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And let's conclude with this. If somebody would suggest that this rule book has introduced the title of chief inspector in the sector for posebna unit, then such claim would not be correct. What have you testified about today is correct. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the posebna unit existed for several decades, the Republic of Macedonia inherited it, so to speak, from the Socialist Federative of Yugoslavia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. When I was employed, I immediately became member of the posebna unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it also correct that those were regular police officers with full employment status in the Ministry of Interior and that they were only deployed in the situations when it was necessary to provide a special safeguarding of the public law and order or when public law and order were disturbed to a greater extent?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the right to perform duties we have several types of security, regular, extraordinary and special. And these two types, extraordinary and special, mean involvement of the posebna unit and recently when an assessment will be made that there will be a disturbance of public law and order these posebna units are activated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters wish for clarification whether it is posebna units or special units. We have an agreement about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Posebna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me now, General, is it correct that the posebna unit was always within the police department?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, within the sector for special tasks. For posebna -- posebna tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me also whether in 2001, during the crisis posebna unit was placed at a permanent state of readiness?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct also that all orders related to posebna were issued within the police department, either by the head of the posebna units, or the under-secretary for uniformed police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct also, if I say that the battalions of the posebna unit or parts of the battalions of the posebna unit were also deployed in accordance with the orders of their superior officers also in some of the battles in the crisis region?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that in the joint operations with the army of the Republic of Macedonia parts of posebna were also placed under the command of the military, of the army commanders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: It is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then the line of command was such that the commander of the battalion of the posebna unit, or of another posebna unit had a direct command over the members of its unit or battalion, or a platoon, while the orders were received from the army superior officers.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. So we received the orders from the army superiors, while the operational superiors, the direct superiors who are managing the units from within the posebna were issuing orders to their own police officers, and the police officers would perform those orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, as the superior of posebna, or as the chief inspector of posebna, were placed under the command of the army superiors in May 2001 in battles around Vaksince. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI
utterances.text: It is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe this would be the appropriate time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We've reached 7.00. We adjourn now for the evening. We resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.,
